name: Via Appia. Regina Viarum
description: The Via Appia, nicknamed the "queen of roads," runs more than 800 kilometres from Rome to Brindisi on Italy's southeast coast. Begun in 312 BCE as a military route south, it later carried trade and helped towns grow along its path. Today you can walk stretches of it past Roman bridges, aqueducts, baths and amphitheatres.
